reason: This text from Exodus 1-2 demonstrates Yahweh's favor toward the Hebrew people, not antagonism. The passage explicitly shows God blessing the Hebrews with multiplication and strength despite Egyptian oppression (וַיִּרְבּוּ וַיַּֽעַצְמוּ בִּמְאֹד מְאֹד - they multiplied and became very strong). God rewards the midwives who fear Him and resist Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew infants (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת - God dealt well with the midwives) and makes them houses. The antagonism in this passage comes from Pharaoh, not from Yahweh. Yahweh is portrayed as protecting the Hebrew people through divine providence, including the rescue and protection of Moses.
